before.text:
Abstract. There has been a surge of interest of late in an old result of Nyman and
                                                         Beurling giving a Hilbert space formulation of the Riemann hypothesis. Many authors
                                                         have contributed to this circle of ideas, culminating in a beautiful refinement due to
                                                         Baez-Duarte. The purpose of this little survey is to dis-entangle the resulting web of
                                                         complications, and reveal the essential simplicity of the main results.

                                                         Keywords.      Riemann hypothesis; Hilbert space; total set; semigroups.

It also notes that any weights bounded above and below by constant multiples of n^2 give isomorphic Hilbert spaces and preserve totality.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The Hardy-space formulation makes two otherwise separate operations compatible: boundary L2 convergence can certify closed-span approximation, while interior point evaluation can later detect an off-line zero.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: On the half-plane Re(s)>1/2, the source defines H^2 and its boundary norm. The generators F_lambda=(lambda^s-lambda)zeta(s)/s are analytic because the factor vanishes at the pole of zeta, and a zeta growth estimate puts them in H^2. Discrete generators G_l=F_{1/l} and E=1/s yield Theorem 2: RH is equivalent to E lying in the closed span of either the discrete or continuous generator family.
directed.conceptual_reading: The representation packages RH as approximate inversion of zeta in a normed analytic space. Analyticity, norm convergence, and continuous evaluation are all preserved, enabling both constructive and obstructive directions.
directed.representation_or_bridge: F_lambda is the bridge object: a dilation difference cancels zeta's pole while retaining every nontrivial zeta zero. H^2 links boundary integrability to interior analytic structure.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The main implication from RH to discrete closure depends on Littlewood-type estimates not yet proved here. Exact Hardy normalization and generator formulas matter.
directed.uncertainty: The proof plan is explicit, but OCR affects fractions and norms; exact normalizations should be scan-checked.

The claim that norm convergence and continuous evaluation are all preserved anticipates later Hardy-space arguments rather than reporting this unit's evidence.
